title: Self-Regulated Reading with AI Support: An Eight-Week Study with Students
extended_summary:
This paper examines how college students use generative AI chatbots to support self-regulated academic reading, and how those interaction patterns relate to cognitive engagement over time. The authors note that while AI tools are increasingly used for reading support, there has been little granular evidence about what students actually do during AI-supported reading sessions, especially across multiple weeks.

The study followed 15 undergraduate students in an introductory AI course at a large public university in the United States over eight weeks. Students completed AI-supported reading logs for their assigned readings, producing 239 reading sessions and 838 prompts. The researchers coded prompts into four cognitive themes — Decoding, Comprehension, Reasoning, and Metacognition — and also conducted interviews with five students plus thematic analysis of optional reflections. There was no non-AI comparison group; instead, the paper focused on characterizing AI use and students’ own perceptions of it.

The findings show that students used AI mostly for comprehension support, especially summaries and explanations, with reasoning prompts less common and metacognitive prompts rare. Most sessions consisted only of the minimum required number of prompts, and prompt engineering techniques were seldom used even after instruction. Cognitive engagement shifted within sessions from comprehension toward reasoning, but overall patterns stayed stable across the eight weeks, with strong individual differences. Qualitative results suggest that efficiency was the main driver of AI use, and that students often used AI summaries to triage what to read more deeply, effectively reading through AI rather than with it. The authors conclude that AI reading systems should better scaffold deeper engagement and caution that instruction alone may be insufficient to change students’ habits without stronger system support.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI chatbot/assistant used for conversational support over text, including summarization, explanation, questioning, and follow-up dialogue.
identified_tools.use_case: Students used AI chatbots of their choice to support self-regulated reading of course assigned texts, asking for summaries, explanations, definitions, implications, comparisons, and other forms of reading support over an eight-week period.

findings.finding_summary: In an eight-week longitudinal study of 15 undergraduates across 239 reading sessions and 838 prompts, students used the AI primarily for comprehension support (59.6% of coded prompts), followed by reasoning (29.8%), metacognition (8.5%), and decoding (2.1%). The paper reports qualitative and descriptive evidence that AI use often improved efficiency and access to understanding, but also encouraged shallow processing, reduced deep engagement, and strategic triage of reading through AI-generated summaries rather than with the original text.
findings.measure: Prompt coding distribution; reading-session logs; interviews and optional reflections

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods longitudinal study with descriptive coding and interviews rather than an experimental comparison. It provides useful evidence about usage patterns, but not causal estimates of learning effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports important behavioral patterns and perceived benefits/costs, but it does not provide measurable learning gains or effect sizes. The impact on literacy learning is therefore suggestive but unclear.
